explain_task.question: Using the revised LP-relaxation diagnostics, explain why the optimal solution keeps all premium variables `y[i][p]` and `v_prem[i][p]` at zero even though premium mode was introduced. Your answer must trace `v_std_0_0 = 30`, `v_std_1_1 = 70`, the binding constraints `volume_balance_0`, `volume_balance_1`, `location_capacity_1`, and `std_only_if_assigned_0_1`, back to the exact CSV columns `Transportation_volume_to_Location_1`, `Transportation_volume_to_Location_2`, `Transportation_cost_to_Location_1`, `Transportation_cost_to_Location_2`, and the parameter values `premium_cost_multiplier = 1.5` and `min_premium_share = 0.4`; also name the exact code variables `x[i][p]`, `y[i][p]`, `v_std[i][p]`, `v_prem[i][p]`, `c_std[(i,p)]`, and `c_prem[(i,p)]`. Then compare the original objective 330.0 to the revised 670.0 by pinpointing which exact code additions in `current_heuristic.py` changed the economics, interpret the shadow prices/duals and slacks in business terms, and explain why you cannot linearly extrapolate the `location_capacity_1` or `volume_balance_1` dual to predict the cost of adding capacity or forcing premium usage.
